- **What was your role at RAVI IIT Delhi?** At RAVI (Reading Assistant for Visually Impaired), I worked as a Software Engineer developing accessibility solutions using computer vision and ML technologies to help visually impaired students access STEM education.

- **Can we collaborate on a project?** Absolutely! I'm always interested in collaborating on innovative projects. You can reach out to me through the contact form or via email at laxmankethavath5@gmail.com

## Learning path

An opinionated roadmap for learning AI, ML and agentic AI engineering, written by K Laxman.
The ordering is the point: LLM fundamentals -> RAG -> Agent loops -> Tools / MCP -> Harness engineering -> Evals + tracing -> Production architecture -> System design.
27 stages, ~66 hours of study plus the builds.

### AI — Understand the model, then ground it in your own data (21h)
https://laxman824.github.io/learn/ai
For: You want to build products on top of LLMs.
The most common job going, and the one with the widest gap between a demo and something you would put in front of a customer. Understand what the model actually is, then learn to feed it your data without it inventing things.

- [LLM fundamentals](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/llms): Understand the thing everything else sits on. ~6h. If you only ever do one item on this page, do the first one. Almost every confused conversation I have about AI systems traces back to someone never having watched this.
- [Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/rag): The part most people do badly. ~10h. Everyone can build a RAG demo in an afternoon. Almost nobody can tell you why theirs returns the wrong chunk. The difference between those two people is this track — and the eval set at the end of it.
- [Evals, tracing & observability](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/evals): The stage everyone skips. ~5h. This is the one that separates a demo from a product. As a system gets complicated, evals and tracing stop being nice-to-have and become the only way you can change anything without breaking it. If…

### ML — The classical craft — rows, columns, and not fooling yourself (15h)
https://laxman824.github.io/learn/ml
For: Your data lives in a database, not in documents.
Quieter than the AI headlines and still what most companies actually need. A table, a column you want to predict, and the discipline to know whether it worked. Boosted trees have not stopped winning just because language models arrived.

- [Classic ML](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/ml-core): Still what wins on the data most companies actually have. ~10h. The half of the job the AI headlines skipped, and the half that quietly pays for most ML salaries: a table of rows, a column you want to predict, and the discipline not to fool yourself about how…
- [Evals, tracing & observability](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/evals): The stage everyone skips. ~5h. This is the one that separates a demo from a product. As a system gets complicated, evals and tracing stop being nice-to-have and become the only way you can change anything without breaking it. If…

### Agentic AI Engineering — A model, in a loop, with tools — and the harness that makes it reliable (34h)
https://laxman824.github.io/learn/agentic
For: You want the thing to do the work, not just answer.
Where I spend my own time, and where the marketing is furthest from the engineering. It is a while loop with an approval gate — the hard parts are the tools, the evaluation and the failure isolation, not the magic. The job title for that…

- [LLM fundamentals](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/llms): Understand the thing everything else sits on. ~6h. If you only ever do one item on this page, do the first one. Almost every confused conversation I have about AI systems traces back to someone never having watched this.
- [Agents & tools](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/agents): A model, in a loop, with tools. That's it. ~17h. This is the track I care most about, because it is the one where the industry's marketing is furthest from the engineering. An agent is not a mysterious autonomous intelligence. It is a while loop…
- [Evals, tracing & observability](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/evals): The stage everyone skips. ~5h. This is the one that separates a demo from a product. As a system gets complicated, evals and tracing stop being nice-to-have and become the only way you can change anything without breaking it. If…
- [Production architecture](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/production): Where AI engineering becomes engineering. ~6h. The gap between a working prototype and a system real users depend on is not model quality. It is latency, failure isolation, cost, caching and observability — ordinary distributed-systems work…

### AI Engineer, interview-ready — Build what AI engineering interviews ask about, then learn to explain it (52h)
https://laxman824.github.io/learn/job
For: You want to be ready to interview for an AI engineering role.
The route I would take if the goal were an AI engineering role rather than a side project. It covers the systems these interviews keep returning to — retrieval, agents, evaluation and running things in production — and finishes on the…

- [LLM fundamentals](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/llms): Understand the thing everything else sits on. ~6h. If you only ever do one item on this page, do the first one. Almost every confused conversation I have about AI systems traces back to someone never having watched this.
- [Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/rag): The part most people do badly. ~10h. Everyone can build a RAG demo in an afternoon. Almost nobody can tell you why theirs returns the wrong chunk. The difference between those two people is this track — and the eval set at the end of it.
- [Agents & tools](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/agents): A model, in a loop, with tools. That's it. ~17h. This is the track I care most about, because it is the one where the industry's marketing is furthest from the engineering. An agent is not a mysterious autonomous intelligence. It is a while loop…
- [Evals, tracing & observability](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/evals): The stage everyone skips. ~5h. This is the one that separates a demo from a product. As a system gets complicated, evals and tracing stop being nice-to-have and become the only way you can change anything without breaking it. If…
- [Production architecture](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/production): Where AI engineering becomes engineering. ~6h. The gap between a working prototype and a system real users depend on is not model quality. It is latency, failure isolation, cost, caching and observability — ordinary distributed-systems work…
- [System design & interview](https://laxman824.github.io/learn/interview): A separate rail — not about building, about being hired. ~8h. This track is honestly part of the path I walked, but it is a different kind of thing to the six above: it is about communicating the work rather than doing it. Pick it up at the end, or in parallel…
